notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Black plates with white characters that blur into three white blocks; commercial vehicles use yellow and newer plates may be white.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Drives on the left.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: White or yellow centre lines with always-white edge lines; yellow centres are rare in older Generation 3 coverage.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Round steel or concrete poles; steel ones are often painted black with flag-coloured bands.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Black-and-white square or round bollards, plus yellow-and-black ones that may carry a red reflector.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Yellow waystones angled toward the road, with a cutout at the top listing three towns, the biggest on top.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Latin-script language with Dutch-influenced spellings; a near twin of the one in Malaysia, which leans toward English spellings.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Rows of red and white banners and flags line many streets.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Cigarette ads priced around 18,000 Rp, with graphic warning images and the word PERINGATAN.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Motorcycles carry front licence plates, unlike in other Southeast Asian countries.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Prices are in rupiah (Rp).

notes.subject: other
notes.text: A Muslim-majority country, so churches and Christian signs point to specific regions.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: No coverage at all in the far east (Papua); coverage is thin in several outer areas.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Addresses use direction words: Utara north, Timur east, Selatan south, Barat west, Tengah central.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Satellite dishes point toward the equatorial belt, so their tilt hints at north or south of the equator.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Five-digit postal codes start with 1 near the capital and rise to 9 in the far east.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Poles with an indent on both sides are found in the west of the main island.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Trident-style pole tops are common in the middle of the main island.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Crossbars with the flat part facing away from the pole are common on Sulawesi.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: White fences painted with blue or red are typical of Sulawesi.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Crown-like roof pinnacles, guardian statues, slit-drum towers and dark carved volcanic-stone gates.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Horizontal text painted on poles, usually dark blue, is a good sign of this island.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Boat-shaped roofs with spires in the west; lower, spire-less ones near the big lake in the north.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Mountains around a big lake with an island in the middle, often under overcast sky.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Elevated houses with saddle-shaped roofs, in a small area of South Sulawesi.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Horizontal slots in the roof triangles are almost unique to South Sulawesi.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Roofs made of wooden chips are found on Borneo.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The Lesser Sunda Islands are drier, with lower, shrubbier, less tropical vegetation.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Tall high-pitched peaked roofs on Sumba, which also has savannah landscapes.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Oil palm plantations are concentrated on Sumatra and Borneo.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Very rounded green hills covered in palms, sugarcane or corn.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Red soil topped with white soil that spills onto the road.
